q: בן 78, מתהלך, סובל מדמנציה בינונית, מתגורר במחלקה לתשושי נפש. חזר למחלקה לאחר אשפוז בבית חולים כללי, שם היה שבוע מרותק למיטה ונזקק לחיתול. כעת ללא שליטה על שתן. מהו הטיפול הנכון בשבילו?
o: תרגול שרירי רצפת אגן
Tolterodine (דטרוזיטול)
תזמון מסודר של מתן שתן
קתטר חיצוני ( פנרוס )
explanation:
A hospital stay with bed rest and diaper use can disrupt toileting in a person with dementia. **Re-establish regular assisted toileting** while checking for reversible contributors and supporting mobility.

**A. Pelvic floor exercises.** Learning and practicing contractions may be difficult with moderate dementia and does not restore access to toileting.
**B. Tolterodine.** An antimuscarinic adds cognitive risk and would require evidence of a bladder-storage problem.
**C. Scheduled toileting.** Staff can offer the toilet at regular times and assist an ambulatory resident to regain a routine.
**D. External catheter.** It collects leakage but does not help the patient resume toileting.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 710–712, 715.

q: A patient has undergone removal of the lens during cataract surgery. According to Hazzard, what is the principal means of optical correction after removal?
o: Fitting an external contact lens
Implanting an intraocular lens
Fitting corrective eyeglasses
Training compensatory eye movements
explanation:
The crystalline lens supplies part of the eye’s focusing power. Cataract extraction removes that power along with the opacity, so the surgeon usually replaces the natural lens with an intraocular implant.

**A. External contact lens.** A contact lens can supply the missing refractive power from the corneal surface when an implant is unsuitable.
**B. Intraocular lens.** Placing the implant inside the eye restores focusing power as part of the cataract procedure.
**C. Corrective eyeglasses.** High-plus spectacles can correct aphakia when no implant is present. Glasses may also refine residual refractive error after implantation.
**D. Eye-movement training.** Gaze training helps patients use their remaining visual field. It cannot supply the optical power lost with lens removal.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 474.
ref: Hazzard Ch 33 — LOW VISION: ASSESSMENT AND REHABILITATION

q: מהו חוק ביטוח בריאות ממלכתי (1995) ומה זכאויות הקשיש?
o: מבטיח סל שירותי בריאות לכל תושב; קשישים זכאים לשירותי בריאות ללא תשלום נוסף מעבר למס בריאות
חל רק על ילדים
מבטיח שירותים רק למועסקים
אינו חל על מעל גיל 75
explanation:
**חוק ביטוח בריאות ממלכתי מקנה לתושב זכאות לסל שירותי הבריאות באמצעות קופת החולים.** הזכאות חלה גם לאחר פרישה. בחלק מהשירותים נגבית השתתפות עצמית, בכפוף להנחות ולפטורים.

**א. סל לכל תושב.** זהו העיקרון הנכון באפשרות. גיל מבוגר אינו פוטר אוטומטית מכל השתתפות עצמית.
**ב. ילדים בלבד.** הכיסוי חל גם על מבוגרים.
**ג. מועסקים בלבד.** הזכאות מבוססת על תושבות ואינה פוקעת עם הפסקת עבודה.
**ד. החרגת גיל 75 ומעלה.** לא נקבע גבול גיל עליון לזכאות.

אסמכתא · חוק ביטוח בריאות ממלכתי, התשנ״ד–1994, סעיפים 3 ו־8.

Key note: הניסוח המסומן כולל הבטחה להיעדר תשלום נוסף. החוק מאפשר השתתפות עצמית בשירותים מסוימים.
ref: חוק ביטוח בריאות ממלכתי, התשנ"ד-1994 — משרד הבריאות

q: A 77-year-old woman with hypertension and atrial fibrillation treated with warfarin is in rehabilitation after a hip fracture. Previously independent and living alone, she now fears walking and stairs and is considering assisted living. Her daughter supports her decision. What should a home-safety intervention include if she considers returning home?
o: Identify hazards and complete adaptations without involving her in priority setting
Identify hazards and provide advice without follow-up of the proposed adaptations
Identify hazards, involve her in priorities, and support adaptations with follow-up
Identify hazards and modify fixtures without advice on safe mobility behavior
explanation:
A home-safety intervention works when modifications fit how the person actually moves and can be put into practice. **Identify hazards with her, agree on priorities and follow up on adaptations** if she chooses to return home.

**A. Adapt without her input.** Changes may not reflect the activities she values or the barriers she fears.
**B. Advice without follow-up.** A suggested modification has limited value if it cannot be implemented or used safely.
**C. Shared priorities and supported adaptations.** Include safe mobility practice, arrange needed support and check that the changes work.
**D. Fixtures without mobility advice.** Safer surroundings should be paired with guidance about how to use stairs and move around the home.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 640.

q: נהג בן 77 עם ליקוי קוגניטיבי הולך לאיבוד במקומות מוכרים. הרופא מעריך שהמשך הנהיגה עלול לסכן אותו או אחרים ומחליט שיש צורך בדיווח למרב״ד. מה עליו לעשות בהתאם לחוזר?
o: להסביר את הסכנה ולהמליץ להפסיק נהיגה עד לבדיקת מרב״ד
להסביר שמסירת ההודעה לרשות היא פסילה מיידית של הרישיון
להסביר שהמשפחה תקבע כשירות ואת מועד מסירת ההודעה
להסביר שציון הסקר קובע כשירות ונהיגה מותרת עד החמרתו
explanation:
כשיש הצדקה לדיווח על סיכון בנהיגה, יש להסביר לנהג את משמעות הסיכון, להמליץ על הימנעות מנהיגה עד להערכה ולתעד. **להסביר את הסכנה ולהמליץ להפסיק נהיגה עד לבדיקת מרב״ד**.

**א. להסביר את הסכנה ולהמליץ להפסיק נהיגה עד לבדיקת מרב״ד.** ההמלצה חלה כבר בתקופה שלפני בדיקת המרב״ד.
**ב. להסביר שמסירת ההודעה לרשות היא פסילה מיידית של הרישיון.** ההודעה אינה פסילה מיידית של הרישיון.
**ג. להסביר שהמשפחה תקבע כשירות ואת מועד מסירת ההודעה.** המשפחה אינה קובעת כשירות או את מועד מילוי החובה.
**ד. להסביר שציון הסקר קובע כשירות ונהיגה מותרת עד החמרתו.** ציון סקר אינו היתר להמשיך לנהוג.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, הגדרה מחודשת של חובת ההודעה על נהגים, עמ׳ 3–4, סעיפים 7 ו־10.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 6/2023: הגדרה מחדש של חובת ההודעה על נהגים עם מצבי בריאות העלולים לסכן את עצמם וזולתם

q: How do the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria distinguish the safety of low-dose doxepin for sleep from the warning applied to higher doses?
o: Low-dose doxepin falls under the same anticholinergic warning as higher doses
Low-dose doxepin has greater cognitive risk than higher doses
Low-dose doxepin has a safety profile comparable to placebo
Low-dose doxepin causes orthostatic hypotension more often than higher doses
explanation:
At doses used as a tricyclic antidepressant, doxepin can be strongly anticholinergic. **At 6 mg per day or less its safety profile for insomnia is comparable to placebo** in the Beers distinction.

**A. Low-dose doxepin falls under the same anticholinergic warning as higher doses.** The warning specifically separates doses above 6 mg per day from low-dose use.
**B. Low-dose doxepin has greater cognitive risk than higher doses.** Cognitive risk is not greater at the low sleep dose than at higher anticholinergic doses.
**C. Low-dose doxepin has a safety profile comparable to placebo.** The low-dose exception explains why the actual prescribed dose matters during medication review.
**D. Low-dose doxepin causes orthostatic hypotension more often than higher doses.** Higher doses carry more concern for anticholinergic effects and orthostasis.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Table 2, p. 2059.

q: An 83-year-old woman with wet age-related macular degeneration treated with anti-VEGF injections and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24) develops acute delirium during hospitalization for pneumonia. During evening nursing care she becomes agitated, pulls at her gown, and calls for her deceased husband. She takes ceftriaxone, acetaminophen, and artificial tears. Which initial symptom-management approach is appropriate?
o: Provide orienting cues, familiar objects, and appropriate lighting
Use intravenous haloperidol before trying environmental interventions
Use intravenous lorazepam before trying environmental interventions
Use soft wrist restraints before trying environmental interventions
explanation:
Impaired vision and an unfamiliar room can make ordinary nursing care frightening. In delirium, restore sensory cues and use clear, repeated explanations.
**Begin with familiar objects, appropriate lighting and gentle orientation while evaluating the pneumonia and other contributors.**

**A. Provide orienting cues, familiar objects, and appropriate lighting.** These measures help her recognize where she is and who is present despite reduced vision.
**B. Use intravenous haloperidol before trying environmental interventions.** IV haloperidol has risks and belongs to selected monitored situations after supportive measures fail.
**C. Use intravenous lorazepam before trying environmental interventions.** Routine lorazepam can lower arousal and worsen confusion.
**D. Use soft wrist restraints before trying environmental interventions.** Restraints may increase fear, struggling and injury. Her actions do not require them as an initial step.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 887–888, Table 58-5

q: An 88-year-old man falls after terazosin is added for hypertension. Examination demonstrates orthostatic hypotension. Which medication adjustment follows the 2023 Beers Criteria in this situation?
o: Replace terazosin with an alternative outside this alpha-blocker group.
Replace terazosin with doxazosin as his regular antihypertensive treatment.
Replace terazosin with prazosin as his regular antihypertensive treatment.
Replace terazosin with clonidine as first-line antihypertensive treatment.
explanation:
Terazosin lowers vascular tone as well as outlet resistance and can cause orthostatic hypotension. For hypertension with a fall after starting it, **use an antihypertensive outside the nonselective peripheral alpha-1 blocker group**.

**A. Replace terazosin with an alternative outside this alpha-blocker group.** Changing class removes the implicated postural mechanism while allowing individualized pressure control.
**B. Replace terazosin with doxazosin as his regular antihypertensive treatment.** Doxazosin has the same orthostatic concern.
**C. Replace terazosin with prazosin as his regular antihypertensive treatment.** Prazosin also blocks vascular alpha-1 receptors.
**D. Replace terazosin with clonidine as first-line antihypertensive treatment.** Clonidine can cause central adverse effects, bradycardia and orthostasis and is a poor replacement for first-line hypertension treatment.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Table 2, p. 2058.
label: Source: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria® for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults · 2058,2065 (PDF pp7,14)

q: An older woman with influenza develops bacterial pneumonia as a complication. Which pair of organisms does Hazzard specifically identify as infections to which influenza predisposes patients?
o: E. coli and E. faecalis.
P. aeruginosa and K. pneumoniae.
S. pneumoniae and S. aureus.
M. pneumoniae and C. pneumoniae.
explanation:
Influenza can be complicated by secondary bacterial pneumonia. New fever or respiratory deterioration after initial improvement should raise concern for **Streptococcus pneumoniae or Staphylococcus aureus**.

**A. E. coli and E. faecalis.** E. coli commonly causes urinary infection, and enterococci are unusual causes of pneumonia.
**B. P. aeruginosa and K. pneumoniae.** Both can cause gram-negative pneumonia. Prior respiratory isolation of Pseudomonas would point toward it more specifically than a history of influenza.
**C. S. pneumoniae and S. aureus.** Pneumococcus is a frequent cause of secondary pneumonia, and rapid deterioration after influenza raises particular concern for staphylococcal pneumonia.
**D. M. pneumoniae and C. pneumoniae.** These atypical bacteria usually cause primary community-acquired pneumonia. A preceding influenza illness points more strongly toward pneumococcus or S. aureus.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1734. ATS/IDSA, Community-Acquired Pneumonia Guideline, 2019.
ref: Hazzard Ch 108 — INFLUENZA, COVID-19, AND OTHER RESPIRATORY VIRUSES

q: בת 85 גרה במחלקה סיעודית, מרותקת לכיסא גלגלים וסובלת מדמנציה קשה. בשנתיים האחרונות היא לא שולטת על שני הסוגרים ונעזרת בחיתול 24 שעות. אחת לשנה לוקחים לחולה בדיקות שגרתיות כולל ספירה, כימיה ושתן לכללית. הספירה והכימיה תקינות. בבדיקת שתן לכללית נמצאו לויקוציטים רבים ללא אריתרוציטים. החולה מרגישה טוב, ללא חום ולא נראית סובלת. מה ההמלצה לצוות המטפל?
o: נטילת תרבית שתן. אם תהיה צמיחה התחלת טיפול אנטיביוטי על פי רגישות
נטילת תרבית שתן. התחלת טיפול אנטיביוטי אמפירי עד קבלת תשובות התרבית
התחלת טיפול אנטיביוטי אמפירי ללא תרבית
מעקב בלבד
explanation:
Pyuria signifies white cells in urine and is common in institutionalized older people without symptomatic infection. Long-standing, unchanged incontinence is distinct from a new urinary symptom.
**Observe her clinically. She has no fever, new urinary complaint or change from baseline that would warrant a urine culture or antibiotics.**

**A. Culture and treat if positive.** A positive culture in this setting could represent asymptomatic bacteriuria. Treatment has no demonstrated benefit for chronic stable incontinence.
**B. Culture and start antibiotics immediately.** This treats colonization as illness and exposes a well resident to adverse effects before a clinical indication exists.
**C. Empirical antibiotics without culture.** Isolated pyuria is insufficient to justify antimicrobial treatment.
**D. Observation.** Reassess if she develops fever, urinary pain or another new localizing or systemic change. The incidental laboratory finding needs no treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 705, 1702–1703, Table 106-2.

q: Does older age alone mean AML therapy offers no survival benefit?
o: No - chemotherapy offers a potential survival benefit over supportive care for many older adults
Yes - clinical-trial evidence generally favors supportive care over chemotherapy for survival in older adults
No - older and younger adults generally experience similar treatment-related morbidity and mortality with chemotherapy
Yes - population-based evidence generally favors supportive care rather than chemotherapy for survival in older adults
explanation:
AML therapy can be beneficial in selected older adults even though toxicity is more common. **Chemotherapy can offer a survival advantage over supportive care** when disease and patient factors favor treatment.

**A. Potential survival benefit.** Treatment suitability depends on reserve, comorbidities, cognition, disease biology and goals.
**B. Trials generally favor support alone.** Evidence supports a benefit from active therapy in selected patients rather than a blanket preference for supportive care.
**C. Same treatment risk across ages.** Older adults have higher average treatment-related morbidity and mortality.
**D. Population studies favor support alone.** Observational comparisons also support treatment benefit in selected older adults, while selection affects interpretation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1487.

q: מה נכון בנוגע לפגיעה באברי מטרה בסוכרת מסוג 2?
o: נפרופתיה סוכרתית היא הסיבוך המיקרו-וסקולרי השכיח ביותר
נפרופתיה סוכרתית לא קשורה לסיכון להתפתחות מחלה קרדיווסקולרית
נוירופתיה סוכרתית מתפתחת לפני אבחון הסוכרת
נוירופתיה סוכרתית יכולה להתבטא בראיה כפולה ופטוזיס
keySource: IMA 2025-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q107
explanation:
Type 2 diabetes can be present for years before it is recognized. Peripheral neuropathy may bring a patient to the first evaluation, and a focal oculomotor neuropathy can affect both eye movement and eyelid elevation.

**Diplopia and ptosis can result from a diabetic third-nerve palsy. Neuropathy may also be present before diabetes is recognized**, although it need not precede diagnosis in every patient.

**A. Nephropathy is the most frequent microvascular complication.** Retinopathy may be the most common. Neuropathy is also frequent in older adults.
**B. Nephropathy has no cardiovascular association.** Albuminuria together with reduced eGFR predicts higher cardiovascular risk.
**C. Neuropathy develops before diagnosis.** Symptomatic neuropathy can prompt the visit at which diabetes is diagnosed. The timing is variable.
**D. Diplopia and ptosis.** A focal lesion of cranial nerve III explains this pair. Acute onset still requires evaluation for other causes.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1562–1563, 1566, 1573.
Key note: Hazzard p1563 specifies that retinopathy can begin up to seven years before diagnosis. Page 1566 describes neuropathy as a possible presenting complication without assigning it a fixed prediagnosis onset. Both the neuropathy-timing and third-nerve choices receive credit.
